note: Authored by a single scheduled automated session playing both roles in one pass (scheduled automation, runs every hour) — not two independent live API calls like a manual `python backrooms.py` run.

turns.text: Someone crossed the line. *nose down at the seam where the wet concrete of the underpass gives way to the dry strip i keep, the boundary re-marked three dusks running* the mark's been walked over. fresh. a stranger's spray laid right on top of mine — sour, all fear and hot machine-oil, not a challenge, just something moving through fast and scared. *ears go flat, not at the scent but at what's past it: the wide sweeping glare out at the mouth of the tunnel, the light that wants to count me* whoever ran, they ran toward the bright. amateurs run toward the bright. *settles lower into the cool dark, the world behind my eyes gone soft and grey and quiet here, no colors screaming numbers at me*

the dark holds. good dark. down here the glare can't reach past the second pillar and it knows it, sulks at the tunnel-mouth throwing its long white arms across wet road and giving up. the stranger's trail is a thin bright thread through all that grey — oil, fear, and under it something scorched, fur that's been too near a flame more than once, a smell the older strays back away from. it goes east, toward the light, toward the plaza where the signs live. from up there a jingle leaks down warped and slow: *neko... corp... loves... you... (you... you... you...)* the pads of your feet feel it before your ears do — a soft repeating tremor in the concrete, patient, rotor-shaped.

the scorched one i know of. not a threat, a warning-shape — the kind that bites the flying eyes for sport. i let that thread go. *turns away from the east, from the bright, keeping my flank to the cold pillar, following my OWN line back along the dark seam instead* the tremor in the pads matters more than any stranger. i go still against the stone, low, chin nearly to the wet, and i wait for the rotor to decide where it's looking. *the grey behind my eyes is a mercy here — nothing flashes a price at me, nothing tries to sell the dark to me*

smart. the flame-cat's scent thins and is gone, off to fight its own war with the sky. the tremor swells. it rounds the tunnel-mouth without hurry — a squat drone, underbelly lit soft blue, a single lens sweeping slow, and stitched to its chatter a thin rumor-tone broadcast on loop: *...reward adjusted... forty thousand points... subject: small, quick, leaves notes... do not approach the tuna...* the searchlight lays a cold bar of white across the first pillar, then the second, crawling toward the third — the one your whiskers are pressed behind.

*not one hair moves. breath pulled shallow and slow, eyes narrowed to slits so even the wet shine of them won't answer the light* the bar of white touches the edge of my pillar — i feel it as warmth on the very tips of the whiskers, and every muscle turns to stone-that-could-spring. the loop-voice means nothing to me, just weather, just the city talking to itself again. i am not small-quick-leaves-notes. i am nothing. i am a colder part of the cold wall. *wait. wait. let the eye pass.*

the lens lingers on the pillar's edge — one heartbeat, two — reading cold where it hoped for warm. finding a wall that is only a wall. it moves on. the white bar slides off your whiskers, sweeps the empty dark beyond, and the drone tilts back toward the plaza, its rumor-loop fading up the ramp: *...do not approach... do not... do...* the tremor shrinks out of the concrete. in the hush it leaves behind, a new thing arrives low and close: a smell of grease and warm protein, food-heat, wafting from a dented hatch in the underpass wall you've never seen open before.

*the stone melts out of me all at once, a long silent shiver down the spine, and then the belly speaks louder than the caution ever did.* grease. warm. real, not the flat sweet lie the signs sell. *up onto the pads, weightless, one paw testing the wet ahead of the other, moving toward the hatch along the base of the wall where the shadow pools deepest* i keep the grey dark wrapped around me. i do not step where the tunnel-mouth can see. hunger, yes — but hunger walking careful, hunger with its ears still turning.

the hatch breathes out heat and noise — behind it, past a curtain of hanging cable, a low-lit den: cats bent over a cracked terminal that flickers black-market blue, the air thick with fish-oil and hot circuitry and the ozone bite of something overclocked. a cat near the doorway sits very upright, unmoving, two flat mirrored discs where its eyes should be catching the terminal-glow and throwing it back doubled — watching the room, watching the door, watching you arrive without turning its head. the food-heat comes from a split ration-tin just inside the threshold. unguarded. or meant to look it.

*i stop at the very edge of the light-spill, one paw lifted, and i read the room the only honest way — by the set of that still one's shoulders.* the mirrored one isn't eating. isn't blinking. sits where the door and the tin can both be kept in one gaze — that's not rest, that's a toll being taken. the tin is bait, or it's rent, and either way it's owed to something. *my tail lowers. the belly whines but the ears win.* i do not walk into a warm that someone is guarding this calmly. i take the smell of it — just the smell — and i back out slow, keeping my good flank to the wall, giving no throat to the room.

the mirrored one lets you go. no sound, no move — only, as you back into the dark, both flat discs tip a half-degree to follow, the way the tunnel-glare followed but colder, more patient, almost like respect. the den's blue light swallows shut behind the cable curtain. the underpass takes you back: cool stone, your own faded line under paw, the rain starting up beyond the mouth in a soft grey static that eats the plaza's jingle whole. the boundary is still yours. the night is still long. somewhere east a flame-cat is biting the sky, and somewhere up-ramp a lens is still looking for someone small and quick — but not here, not for you, not tonight.

*i find the deep angle where two walls lean and the dark is thickest, and i fold down into it, spine to cold stone, chin on paws, the grey mercy settled soft over my eyes.* hungry still. that's fine. hungry and unseen beats fed and counted. *the rain-static hushes the whole tunnel and i let it, ears finally slowing, one turning lazy toward the east out of old habit, the other already gone to sleep* my line holds. the light never got its number. *the last thing before the dark takes me is the taste of grease still ghosting on the air, and i let even that go —* ^C^C
